# Cashflow card lab

<!-- Generated by scripts/card-lab.js from docs/domain/strategy/data/card-results.json - do not edit by hand. -->

What each card is worth, measured. Every card was put in front of **142 typical positions** (taken out of simulated games at roll 3, 10, 20, 32, for every profession, played by the "all-rounder" strategy) and of **93 built-up positions** (the best strategy found, roll 20, 40 and 60, with properties already owned). Each position was played out 20 times with the card taken and 20 times without it, on the same dice. A Deal is "taken" by buying it, a Doodad by paying it, a Market card by playing it. **Effects are in percentage points of the chance to escape the rat race** (plus helps, minus hurts); the measuring error is about one point. Card ids are those of [CASHFLOW_CARDS.md](CASHFLOW_CARDS.md), and the history names a picked card by the same id.

How to use it when you analyse a game: look up the card ids in the history, find them here, and say what the card was worth *in the position the player was in* - a Big Deal bought with a loan is a very different card from the same Big Deal bought from cash. The analyst (`GET /game/review`) measures the player's own decision on the player's own position; this is the background to quote beside it.

Columns: **from cash** - the deposit was in cash on hand; **with a loan** - the bank had to lend it; **rolls saved** - median rolls to escape without the card minus with it, from cash, in a typical / a built-up game; **traded** (shares) - the shares are sold when the price is high.

## How games end in bankruptcy

12000 games with the all-round strategy, 1907 (16%) went bankrupt. The last decision before the end:

- doodad: 61%
- pass: 26%
- market: 9%
- sell: 3%
- repay: 0%
- buy: 0%

The Doodads and Market cards most often among the last three decisions:

- You renovate your kitchen (doodad, `classic-doodad-kitchen`): 11% of the bankruptcies
- You buy your child their first car (doodad, `classic-doodad-firstcar`): 6% of the bankruptcies
